key_insight: A cognitively grounded small language model framework can generate more clinically realistic SUD patient dialogue by aligning responses with latent patient states like beliefs, coping strategies, and readiness to change.
clinical_relevance: This could support more believable and context-aware simulation tools for SUD counseling research, training, and evaluation in resource-constrained settings.
method: Two-stage pipeline: cognitive component detection, then cognitive component-aligned dialogue generation
Knowledge distillation from high-capacity teacher models to train smaller models
Preference optimization with human annotations plus attention-guided reward shaping
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated with BERTScore, ROUGE, METEOR, BLEU, and LLM-as-judge hit metrics, showing stronger cognitive realization and alignment than generic instruction-tuned and mental-health-specific SLM baselines.
watch_item: The framework still depends on high-quality annotations and automated/LLM-based evaluation, so real-world clinical validity and robustness need careful validation before deployment.
paper_title: Multi-Objective Aligned Small Language Model Framework for SUD Patient Dialogue Generation
